mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 440i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series 440i engine replacement typically costs £2,000-£3,800 for a used unit, £3,800-£6,000 for a reconditioned engine, and £4,500-£7,000 for a fully rebuilt B58B30M0 with warranty. Supply-only prices exclude fitting - budget an additional £700-£1,100 for specialist labour.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW 440i B58 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the B58 is widely regarded as one of the most reliable modern BMW engines. It has few catastrophic failure modes and is known for its robust construction, strong tuning potential, and longevity. However, it does have known maintenance items including coolant leaks, oil filter housing gasket leaks, and PCV diaphragm failure.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of B58 engine problems in a BMW 440i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of B58 issues include: coolant loss (check the reservoir regularly), oil leaks around the valve cover or oil filter housing, whistling sounds from the engine (PCV diaphragm failure), rough idle or power loss (VANOS solenoid issues), and blue or white smoke from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 440i?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a typical 440i valued at £12,000-£28,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,500-£7,000 represents a significant but justifiable investment - especially if the car is otherwise in good condition. The B58 is a desirable engine, and the 440i is a car that retains value well. For most owners, replacement makes financial sense.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 440i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 4 Series 440i engine replacement takes 1-2 days for a specialist workshop, assuming the replacement engine is already available. The B58 is a well-understood engine with good parts availability, though the inline-six configuration requires careful installation.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 440i and the M440i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 440i (F32/F33/F36, 2016-2020) uses the B58B30M0 engine producing 326hp. The M440i (G22/G23/G26, 2020-present) uses the newer B58B30B engine producing 374hp (or 387hp with the MHT mild-hybrid system in later models). The M440i also features a more aggressive chassis setup, M Sport differential, and cosmetic upgrades - but both share the same fundamental B58 engine architecture.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement BMW 4 Series 440i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 4 Series 440i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry a shorter warranty (30-90 days), so always confirm the terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 440i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 4 Series 440i was introduced in 2016 as the replacement for the 435i, bringing BMW's new B58 engine to the 4 Series range. Powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six, the 440i delivered a significant leap in performance and refinement over its predecessor while establishing itself as one of the most desirable engines in the BMW lineup. The 440i nameplate was discontinued in 2020 when the G22 generation 4 Series was launched, replaced by the M440i.

milestones.description: F32/F33 440i launched with B58B30M0 3.0L inline-six turbo petrol, 326hp
F36 Gran Coupe 440i joins the range with the same B58B30M0 engine
440i xDrive variant introduced, adding four-wheel drive
LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) facelift introduced; 440i continues with B58B30M0
F32/F33/F36 generation ends; 440i nameplate discontinued, replaced by M440i with B58B30B

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 440i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 4 Series 440i is powered by the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six - widely regarded as one of the most reliable engines BMW has ever produced. The B58 represents a significant evolution from the N55, featuring a stronger closed-deck block, improved cooling, and a more robust timing chain design. While the B58 has few catastrophic failure modes, it does have well-documented maintenance items that emerge with age and mileage. Rebuilt B58 engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks - Why the BMW 4 Series 440i B58 Engine Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B58's cooling system has several known weak points. The water pump can develop leaks, the coolant expansion tank and its cap can fail, and the plastic coolant fittings and hoses can become brittle with age. In some cases, coolant loss can lead to overheating and, if ignored, head gasket failure.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if coolant loss is minor and cap is the cause

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump and fresh coolant
Water pump, thermostat, hoses, expansion tank
repairOptions.longevity: Best for higher-mileage cars as preventative maintenance
Only if engine has overheated and sustained damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 4 Series 440i (2016-2020) is currently valued at approximately £12,000-£28,000 depending on mileage, condition, and body style (Coupe vs Gran Coupe vs Convertible) `[THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader 2025]`. With a rebuilt engine costing £4,500-£7,000 supply-only, replacement cost represents roughly 16-58% of vehicle value. For most 440i examples, a full engine replacement is comfortably justified given the car's retained value. Cooling system repairs are relatively modest and almost always worth doing.
problems.recommendation: The B58's cooling system issues are well-understood and generally inexpensive to fix relative to the value of the car. If you notice coolant levels dropping, have the system pressure-tested immediately. Replacing the water pump and expansion tank preventatively at around 80,000 miles is a sensible investment that can prevent overheating damage. The B58 is too good an engine to scrap over a coolant leak - repair it.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B58B30M0 BMW 4 Series 440i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover Gasket & Oil Filter Housing
problems.rootCause: The valve cover gasket can harden and crack due to heat cycling, leading to oil leaks around the top of the engine. The oil filter housing gasket is another common failure point, with oil seeping from the housing area. In some cases, oil can contaminate the cooling system via the oil filter housing, causing further issues.

repairOptions.longevity: Only if oil starvation has caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above - a typical 440i values at £12,000-£28,000. Oil leak repairs are modest compared to the vehicle's value and are almost always worth doing.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the B58 are generally not catastrophic if caught early. The valve cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket are wearable items that should be replaced when leaks are detected. Regular visual inspections under the bonnet can catch these issues before they escalate. If you smell burning oil or see oil spots on your driveway, have the gaskets inspected promptly.

problems.group: PCV Valve Diaphragm Failure & VANOS Solenoid Wear
problems.h4: PCV Valve Diaphragm Failure & VANOS Solenoid Wear
problems.rootCause: The PCV (crankcase ventilation) system in the B58 has a diaphragm that can rupture, particularly on pre-2019 engines. This can cause blue or white smoke from the exhaust, whistling sounds, and oil consumption. The VANOS solenoids can also suffer from O-ring degradation, leading to rough idle, power loss, and check engine lights.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV diaphragm (aftermarket repair kit available)

repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rough idle or power loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace entire valve cover (later B58s have integrated PCV)
repairOptions.longevity: Required if PCV is integrated and diaphragm has failed
Only if neglected and engine has suffered damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above - a typical 440i values at £12,000-£28,000. PCV and VANOS repairs are relatively modest and almost always worth doing.
problems.recommendation: PCV diaphragm failure is one of the most common B58 issues and, fortunately, one of the cheapest to fix if caught early. On pre-2019 engines, an aftermarket PCV repair kit is available for around £50-£100, making this a very cost-effective repair. If you notice whistling sounds or smoke from the exhaust, get the PCV system checked immediately. VANOS solenoid replacement is also straightforward and well-understood by BMW specialists.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Minor Issues Write Off Your BMW 4 Series 440i
finalCta.paragraph: The B58 engine in the 440i is one of the most robust and reliable modern BMW engines - but it's not maintenance-free. Cooling system leaks, oil leaks, and PCV diaphragm failure are all well-understood issues that can be fixed relatively inexpensively if caught early. The 440i is a car worth preserving; its value and driving experience justify proper maintenance. If the worst happens and you need a replacement, EnginesMarket connects you with vetted UK specialists who can supply a rebuilt B58 with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty - at a fraction of main dealer prices.
